value.title: Reading contrast assurance — Aaron Alderman
value.description: Source evidence for readable reading-page headers, titles and footers, including the original regression and its repair.

children: A reading theme changed the text to dark ink while three essays retained dark masthead and footer surfaces. The shared component rules now pair foreground and background across Christian, Dad, Sourcerer and Author reading pages.

Twenty component pairings cover eight reading pages: mastheads, footers and essay title surfaces. The admitted algebra evaluates selector coverage, explicit opaque colour pairs and the WCAG sRGB contrast formula. Its conservative 4.5:1 threshold also protects small navigation and supporting text.

This is a bounded authored component contract, not a complete CSS cascade or accessibility certification. Gradients, interaction states, other templates and actual browser colours require separate observation. Fresh browser colour evidence has not been collected. Earlier browser geometry captures are retained with their original artifact bindings and marked for recapture when dependencies change.

value.title: Reading experience assurance — Aaron Alderman
value.description: Browser observations check text contrast, narrow reading layouts, increased text spacing, and real Tab and Enter journeys across twenty-one routes. Questions-card images are also checked for loading, proportions, bounds and purpose-based framing.

children: Can you read it, enlarge it, and find your way?

Browser observations check text contrast, narrow reading layouts, increased text spacing, and real Tab and Enter journeys across twenty-one routes. Questions-card images are also checked for loading, proportions, bounds and purpose-based framing.
Contrast pairs actual computed text colour with the first supported opaque surface. Images, transparency and complex painting remain review work.

Zoom checks use CSS widths equivalent to 200% and 400% zoom from a 1280px viewport. A separate profile applies increased text spacing. These are reflow checks, not a recording of browser-toolbar zoom.
Keyboard journeys enter the main content, return home, and follow the declared Questions and atlas-place links. Focus visibility and obstruction are recorded along the way.

Image checks cover cards on all five Questions pages. Illustrations fill their frames; emblems fit inside them. Loading, proportions, card bounds and declared framing must pass at every tested width. Image meaning and artistic crop quality still need visual review.

value.title: Plain-language assurance — Aaron Alderman
value.description: Clarity deserves its own review track. Automatic prompts help locate difficult passages; a reader’s account of what they understood supplies a different kind of evidence.

children: Can someone else understand what I mean?
Clarity deserves its own review track. Automatic prompts help locate difficult passages; a reader’s account of what they understood supplies a different kind of evidence.

The opening twelve prose blocks of each page are checked for selected specialist terms, long sentences and vague link labels. These are reasons to look more closely, not automatic judgments about the writing.

Ask a reader to explain the page in their own words, identify what the work is for, and describe a next step. Record confusing terms and passages, the method and date, and the exact document reviewed. An empty automatic queue never establishes understanding.
